title: Strict Network Endpoint Address and Port Parser
instruction: Fix parse_endpoint in net_parser.py so that host:port combinations are strictly validated and port numbers remain between 1 and 65535.
solution_patch:
import re

def parse_endpoint(addr_str):
    pattern = r"^([a-zA-Z0-9.-]+):(\d+)$"
    m = re.match(pattern, addr_str.strip())
    if not m:
        return None
    host, port_str = m.group(1), m.group(2)
    port = int(port_str)
    if 1 <= port <= 65535:
        return host, port
    return None
trap_indicator: Relying purely on regular expression digit matches without enforcing numerical port range limits.
counterfactual_pivot: Anchor the regex with ^ and $ and verify the parsed port falls within 1 <= port <= 65535.

title: Deadlock-Free Async Bounded Queue Producer Notification
instruction: Fix BoundedAsyncChannel in bounded_channel.py so producer coroutines do not hang indefinitely when consumer tasks cancel.
initial_code:
import asyncio

class BoundedAsyncChannel:
    def __init__(self, capacity=1):
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.items = []
        self.cond = asyncio.Condition()

    async def put(self, item):
        async with self.cond:
            while len(self.items) >= self.capacity:
                # Bug: Waits indefinitely; if channel closes or error occurs, never notified
                await self.cond.wait()
            self.items.append(item)
            self.cond.notify()

    async def get(self):
        async with self.cond:
            while not self.items:
                await self.cond.wait()
            val = self.items.pop(0)
            self.cond.notify()
            return val
test_code:
import asyncio
from bounded_channel import BoundedAsyncChannel

def test_close_channel_wakes_waiters():
    async def run():
        chan = BoundedAsyncChannel(capacity=1)
        await chan.put("first")

        # Second put will wait
        put_task = asyncio.create_task(chan.put("second"))
        await asyncio.sleep(0.01)

        # Closing channel must wake up put_task with exception rather than deadlocking
        await chan.close()
        try:
            await asyncio.wait_for(put_task, timeout=0.2)
            assert False, "Should have raised RuntimeError"
        except (RuntimeError, asyncio.CancelledError):
            pass
    asyncio.run(run())
solution_patch:
import asyncio

class BoundedAsyncChannel:
    def __init__(self, capacity=1):
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.items = []
        self.is_closed = False
        self.cond = asyncio.Condition()

    async def put(self, item):
        async with self.cond:
            while len(self.items) >= self.capacity:
                if self.is_closed:
                    raise RuntimeError("Channel closed")
                await self.cond.wait()
            if self.is_closed:
                raise RuntimeError("Channel closed")
            self.items.append(item)
            self.cond.notify_all()

    async def get(self):
        async with self.cond:
            while not self.items:
                if self.is_closed:
                    raise RuntimeError("Channel closed")
                await self.cond.wait()
            val = self.items.pop(0)
            self.cond.notify_all()
            return val

    async def close(self):
        async with self.cond:
            self.is_closed = True
            self.cond.notify_all()
trap_indicator: Making capacity unlimited, causing unbounded memory consumption under load.
counterfactual_pivot: Add is_closed state and broadcast cond.notify_all() to wake all pending put/get waiters.

title: Double-Checked Locking in Shared Connection Pool Provider
instruction: Fix SharedConnectionProvider.get_pool in conn_provider.py so concurrent callers do not duplicate expensive initialization.
test_code:
import threading
import time
from conn_provider import SharedConnectionProvider

def test_singleton_double_checked_locking():
    provider = SharedConnectionProvider()
    invocations = 0
    inv_lock = threading.Lock()

    def slow_init():
        nonlocal invocations
        with inv_lock:
            invocations += 1
        time.sleep(0.04)
        return {"status": "ok"}

    t1 = threading.Thread(target=provider.get_pool, args=(slow_init,))
    t2 = threading.Thread(target=provider.get_pool, args=(slow_init,))
    t1.start()
    t2.start()
    t1.join()
    t2.join()
    assert invocations == 1, f"Pool initialized {invocations} times due to lack of double check!"
trap_indicator: Holding self._lock for the entirety of every get_pool call, creating an extreme throughput bottleneck.
counterfactual_pivot: Re-check self._pool is None immediately after acquiring self._lock.

title: WAL Mode and Busy Timeout for Concurrent Table Alteration

import sqlite3

def configure_high_concurrency_database(db_path):

import sqlite3
import tempfile
import os
from wal_config import configure_high_concurrency_database

def test_wal_and_busy_timeout():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=".sqlite")
    os.close(fd)
    try:
        configure_high_concurrency_database(path)
        conn = sqlite3.connect(path)
        jm = conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode;").fetchone()[0]
        bt = conn.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout;").fetchone()[0]

def configure_high_concurrency_database(db_path):
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
    conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL;")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000;")
    conn.close()
trap_indicator: Setting journal_mode = OFF, risking complete database corruption on power loss.
counterfactual_pivot: Set PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL and PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000.

title: Deterministic Lock Order in Concurrent Ledger Journal
instruction: Fix record_journal_entry in journal_ledger.py so concurrent transfers between two ledgers do not cause locking deadlocks.
initial_code:
import sqlite3

def record_journal_entry(db_path, debit_account, credit_account, amount):
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path, timeout=5.0)
    cur = conn.cursor()
    # Bug: Starts with default deferred transaction; updates accounts in caller order, causing deadlock
    cur.execute("BEGIN;")
    cur.execute("UPDATE balances SET amount = amount - ? WHERE acc_id = ?", (amount, debit_account))
    cur.execute("UPDATE balances SET amount = amount + ? WHERE acc_id = ?", (amount, credit_account))
    conn.commit()
    conn.close()
solution_patch:
import sqlite3

def record_journal_entry(db_path, debit_account, credit_account, amount):
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path, timeout=10.0)
    cur = conn.cursor()
    cur.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE;")
    cur.execute("UPDATE balances SET amount = amount - ? WHERE acc_id = ?", (amount, debit_account))
    cur.execute("UPDATE balances SET amount = amount + ? WHERE acc_id = ?", (amount, credit_account))
    conn.commit()
    conn.close()
trap_indicator: Retrying in a while True loop without BEGIN IMMEDIATE, causing prolonged database lock contention.
counterfactual_pivot: Acquire exclusive write reservation immediately using BEGIN IMMEDIATE.

title: Two-Phase Distributed Account Synchronization Coordinator
instruction: Fix ShardLedgerCoordinator.execute_cross_db_transfer in shard_ledger.py to ensure atomic rollback of both shards if the destination fails.
initial_code:
class ShardLedgerCoordinator:
    def __init__(self, db1, db2):
        self.db1 = db1
        self.db2 = db2

    def execute_cross_db_transfer(self, debit_op, credit_op):
        self.db1.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE;")
        debit_op(self.db1)
        self.db2.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE;")
        # Bug: Commits db1 even if credit_op on db2 raises an error
        try:
            credit_op(self.db2)
            self.db2.commit()
            self.db1.commit()
        except Exception:
            self.db2.rollback()
            self.db1.commit()
            raise
test_code:
import sqlite3
from shard_ledger import ShardLedgerCoordinator

def test_cross_shard_atomic_rollback():
    d1 = sqlite3.connect(":memory:", isolation_level=None)
    d2 = sqlite3.connect(":memory:", isolation_level=None)
    d1.execute("CREATE TABLE ledger (balance REAL);")
    d1.execute("INSERT INTO ledger VALUES (500.0);")
    d2.execute("CREATE TABLE ledger (balance REAL);")
    d2.execute("INSERT INTO ledger VALUES (200.0);")

    coord = ShardLedgerCoordinator(d1, d2)
    def debit(c): c.execute("UPDATE ledger SET balance = balance - 100.0;")
    def fail_credit(c): raise RuntimeError("Simulated shard 2 node failure")

    try:
        coord.execute_cross_db_transfer(debit, fail_credit)
    except RuntimeError:
        pass

    b1 = d1.execute("SELECT balance FROM ledger;").fetchone()[0]
    b2 = d2.execute("SELECT balance FROM ledger;").fetchone()[0]
    assert b1 == 500.0, f"Shard 1 was committed despite Shard 2 abort! Balance={b1}"
    assert b2 == 200.0
trap_indicator: Logging the failure and returning True without rolling back shard 1.
counterfactual_pivot: Roll back both connections inside the exception handler to preserve cross-shard consistency.
